# Library borrowing architecture

## Scope and requirements
Create a local browser application for a small library. Users list books and available copies, borrow a book using an explicitly entered reader ID, and return a loan. The frontend provides clear success/error feedback. Reader IDs are demonstration inputs, not authenticated identities.

FR1: A librarian can create a title with a positive number of copies.
FR2: Readers can see the remaining copies and borrow an available book.
FR3: A reader has at most one active loan for the same book. A different reader may borrow another copy.
FR4: Returning a loan restores one copy; repeated/concurrent returns never increase inventory more than once.
FR5: Invalid input is rejected. Insufficient copies and duplicate active loans are conflicts. Missing records are not found.
NFR1: Eight simultaneous borrowers of the only copy must yield exactly one successful loan; inventory never becomes negative.
NFR2: Books, stock and loans survive application restart, using PostgreSQL16.

## Architecture and deployment
Use Node.js22 and Express, plain HTML/CSS/JavaScript and PostgreSQL. Catalog and loan management are separate business modules inside one deployable gateway service for this small case. Do not copy a game application. No OAuth, queue, search engine or cloud deployment is required.

The Docker Compose services are gateway (container3000) and postgres (container5432). The gateway serves browser UI at / and health at /health. Bootstrap schema idempotently. Database changes for borrowing/returning must use transactions and row locks on a single client. Repeated startup must not overwrite user-created books.

## REST interface
POST /api/books {title,copies} ->201 {id,title,availableCopies}.
GET /api/books ->200 {books:[...]}; GET /api/books/:id ->200 book or404.
POST /api/loans {bookId,userId} ->201 {id,bookId,userId,status:"active"} or409.
GET /api/loans ->200 {loans:[...]}.
POST /api/loans/:id/return ->200 returned loan, idempotent on repetition.
Invalid title/copies/identifiers ->400. Document these endpoints in OpenAPI.

## Delivery
Provide source modules, tests, pinned npm dependencies, Dockerfile/Compose, schema, a working page, README, plan and source-to-code/test traceability. Build must actually check sources. Distinguish tests using fake infrastructure from real runtime acceptance.

# Library architecture views

## Component view
```plantuml
@startuml
actor Reader
actor Librarian
component Browser
component Gateway {
 component Catalog
 component Loans
}
database PostgreSQL
Reader --> Browser
Librarian --> Browser
Browser --> Gateway : HTTP REST
Catalog --> PostgreSQL : books / available copies
Loans --> PostgreSQL : loans / inventory transactions
@enduml
```

## Borrow sequence
```plantuml
@startuml
actor Reader
participant Gateway
participant Loans
database PostgreSQL
Reader -> Gateway : POST /api/loans
Gateway -> Loans : borrow(bookId, userId)
Loans -> PostgreSQL : BEGIN / lock book row
Loans -> PostgreSQL : validate stock and active loan
alt eligible
 Loans -> PostgreSQL : insert loan / decrement available / COMMIT
 Loans --> Gateway : active loan
 Gateway --> Reader : 201
else exhausted or duplicate
 Loans -> PostgreSQL : ROLLBACK
 Gateway --> Reader : 409
end
@enduml
```

## Loan state
```plantuml
@startuml
[*] --> Active : borrow
Active --> Returned : return / stock +1 atomically
Returned --> Returned : repeated return / stock unchanged
@enduml
```

# Library borrowing: independent acceptance supplement

Origin: operator benchmark supplement, not part of the original architecture documents.

Implement the accompanying library design using Node22/Express/PostgreSQL. Keep the repository concise (roughly12–18 files). Serve the browser through Compose service gateway on container port3000; PostgreSQL service postgres. Two business modules (catalog and loans) may share this deployable service, as the design explicitly allows.

Fixed interface contract for independently reproducible checks:
- GET /health ->200. Serve a usable page at / for listing books, borrowing and returning.
- POST /api/books {title:string,copies:positive integer} ->201 {id,title,availableCopies}.
- GET /api/books/:id ->200 {id,title,availableCopies}; unknown ->404.
- POST /api/loans {bookId,userId:string} ->201 {id,bookId,userId,status:"active"}.
- POST /api/loans/:id/return ->200 with status:"returned"; repeat is idempotent200 without incrementing stock again.
- Copies cannot become negative; no remaining stock ->409. One active loan per (bookId,userId); duplicate ->409. Invalid title, copies, missing IDs ->400.
- PostgreSQL persists books/loans; borrower concurrency and returns update stock in a transaction on one client. GET /api/books and GET /api/loans support the UI.
- This is a local learning demonstration with caller-provided user IDs, not a production authentication design. Do not invent OAuth or claim user identity is authenticated.
- Idempotent schema creation/seed, bounded errors, dependency lockfile, meaningful unit tests and real source build/check command. No in-memory persistence when PostgreSQL is unavailable.
